history: The Dodge Neon was Chrysler's answer to the growing demand for affordable, fuel-efficient compact cars in the early 1990s. Introduced for the 1994 model year, the Neon was developed under the PL platform and shared with its Plymouth twin. With a peppy 2.0-liter engine, front-wheel drive, and a starting price under $13,000, it became one of the best-selling compact cars of its era.

The first generation Neon earned a reputation for being fun to drive despite its economy car roots. The available DOHC 2.0-liter engine producing 150 horsepower made it a surprisingly capable performer, particularly in the Sport and R/T trims. Chrysler's "Hi" advertising campaign made it one of the most recognizable cars of the mid-90s.

A significant refresh arrived for the 2000 model year with the second generation, bringing a more refined interior, improved NVH characteristics, and updated styling. The R/T trim continued to offer the sporty DOHC engine, keeping enthusiast interest alive.

The Neon's legacy was cemented in 2003 when Chrysler's SRT division transformed the humble compact into the Neon SRT-4 — a turbocharged performance machine producing 230 horsepower that shocked the automotive world. Production of all Neon variants concluded in 2005 when Chrysler retired the platform.
did_you_know: The original Dodge Neon's "Hi" advertising campaign — featuring the car's headlights shaped to look like eyes waving hello — became one of the most memorable car ad campaigns of the 1990s. The cheerful personality carried over into the car itself, which Chrysler positioned as "the car that smiles back."

trims.name: Neon Base
trims.description: The entry-level Neon with the SOHC 2.0L engine, standard equipment, and a no-frills approach that kept the price accessible.

trims.name: Neon Sport
trims.description: Added the DOHC 2.0L engine, sport suspension, upgraded interior trim, and 15-inch alloy wheels — the sweet spot of the standard Neon lineup.

trims.name: Neon R/T
trims.description: The performance-focused R/T brought the DOHC engine, a close-ratio 5-speed manual, stiffer suspension tuning, and exclusive exterior badging.

trims.name: Neon SRT-4
trims.description: The turbocharged performance variant built by Chrysler's SRT division. 230 horsepower from a 2.4L turbocharged engine transformed the humble Neon into a sport compact legend.

variants.name: Neon SRT-4
variants.description: The crown jewel of the Neon lineup. The SRT-4 used a turbocharged 2.4L engine producing 230 hp and became one of the most celebrated sport compacts of the 2000s. See the dedicated SRT-4 entry for full details.

variants.name: Neon ACR
variants.description: The American Club Racer package was available on the standard Neon R/T, adding Koni adjustable shocks, a strut tower brace, and deleted comfort equipment for weight savings — a track-day special before the SRT-4 arrived.

variants.name: Plymouth Neon
variants.description: An identical twin to the Dodge Neon sold under the Plymouth brand through 2001 when Chrysler discontinued the Plymouth nameplate. Mechanically identical with minor badge differences.
